segments.text: OK, so let's go over the seminar we have this week on the causes of poverty.
Could you summarize what ideas were discussed by the group?
Well, some people thought that living in poverty is the fault of the individual, whether you
It's up to each person to take the opportunities that come along in life to work hard and
aim for a good standard of living.
You can't blame anyone else but yourself if you don't succeed in making a good life
for yourself? Yes, but the other view is the opposite. This view sees poverty as a result
of circumstances beyond the individual's control. For example, someone born into the
slums of, for example, Mumbai in India, wouldn't necessarily find any opportunities in an environment
that is so poor. So they may never find a way to make their situation in life any better.
Good. And what conclusions were reached at the end of the seminar?
Well, the conclusion was that poverty is probably caused by a mixture of factors, rather than
any single one on its own. This means the individual person and the environment they
live in may result in them living a life of poverty.
Yes, and it could also mean we should consider a range of other matters, such as government
policy, international relations and so on. Well done. That's all for this tutorial.
It's been very interesting talking to you both and good luck with your studies.
